one_liner: Small embeddable C++ bytecode VM for a Lua-like language with classes; ran fib(34) about 4.5x faster than Duktape 1.2.2 in 2015.
what_it_does: Squirrel is a dynamically typed, imperative/OO scripting language (C-like syntax, tables, arrays, classes with inheritance, delegation, generators, coroutine 'threads', exceptions) whose compiler and VM are a few thousand lines of C++ behind a C API. The host creates a VM with sq_open, compiles source with sq_compilebuffer (or loads precompiled bytecode), and drives it through a Lua-style value stack (sq_push*/sq_get*/sq_call); native functions are registered with sq_newclosure. It is not a drop-in for Duktape: scripts must be written in Squirrel, not JavaScript.
how_it_is_fast: Source is compiled to a register-based bytecode (each SQInstruction carries a target and up to three operand registers or a 32-bit immediate) executed by a single switch-dispatched loop in SQVM::Execute. Values are tagged unions (type plus value), so integers and floats are unboxed, and the arithmetic macros take a fast path when both operands are integers or floats. Memory is reference counted, so most objects are freed immediately with no GC pauses; an optional mark-and-sweep pass for cycles only runs when the host calls sq_collectgarbage. Nothing here is unusual for a bytecode VM; the gap to Duktape 1.2.2 says as much about Duktape's slow interpreter as about Squirrel.
when_to_use: Games or real-time C++ applications that want a compact scripting VM with no GC pauses (reference counting plus an explicit, host-triggered cycle collector).
Script authors who prefer C/JavaScript-like syntax with built-in classes and inheritance over Lua's tables-and-metatables.
Embedding on Windows, Linux, FreeBSD, Illumos or ARM boards from source or via the vcpkg/Conan packages, including compiler-less builds (NO_COMPILER) that only run precompiled bytecode.
Several independent interpreters in one process (each sq_open creates its own shared state), or many cooperative coroutines inside one VM via sq_newthread.
when_not_to_use: Raw interpreter speed is the priority: on the same Scriptorium table PUC Lua (1.341 s), Wren (1.997 s) and AngelScript (2.039 s) beat Squirrel (2.126 s) on fib(34), and LuaJIT is far ahead.

Running untrusted scripts or bytecode: the issue tracker has open, unanswered memory-safety reports from 2026 (#315 'Out Of Bounds Access Leads to Sandbox Breakout', #324 to #327 heap and stack buffer overflows in bytecode loading and format validation, #310 to #312 compiler overflows).
You need responsive upstream maintenance: commits are sparse (Nov 2024, then one merged pull request on 2026-02-28) and about 91 issues are open.
Floating-point-heavy code with default settings: SQFloat is a 32-bit float unless SQUSEDOUBLE is defined, and that switch is not in the build documentation.

Host-to-script call overhead is the bottleneck: taksatou/embench (i7-2600S, Linux) measured 100000 echo calls at 22.3 ms for Squirrel versus 15.2 ms for Lua and 12.5 ms for LuaJIT, though Squirrel was slightly faster than Lua on its 'invert' test (480.0 vs 505.4 ms).

integration.form: static lib or shared lib (libsquirrel + sqstdlib via CMake), or source-drop of the squirrel/ and sqstdlib/ .cpp files
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 per CMakeLists (CMake 3.12+); README lists MSVC 6.0 to 12.0 and gcc 3.2 to 5.3.1 as confirmed; builds with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti on GCC
integration.platforms: Windows (x86, amd64), Linux (x86, amd64, ARM), Illumos, FreeBSD (x86, ARM); _SQ64 is auto-defined for _WIN64/_LP64
integration.thread_safety: Not documented as thread-safe. Each sq_open VM has its own SQSharedState, so separate VMs can live on separate threads; friend VMs from sq_newthread share that state (non-atomic reference counts) and are coroutines, not concurrent threads.

gotchas: Harness limits behind the 4.5x: Scriptorium's bench.exe times five whole-process system() launches (start-up included) and never checks the printed result, and the test is a single recursive fib(34) in which fibR is a root-table global (a table lookup per call; the JavaScript and Lua versions are globals too). The 2.126 s Squirrel and 9.544 s Duktape rows come from the same alphabetical pass in bench.csv (lines 49 to 81), but the first pass gave 4.114 s versus 14.30 s (about 3.5x), so session noise moved the ratio by about a quarter. The timed build was Squirrel 3.0.7 (built with cl /Ox /Oy /MT /DNDEBUG), not today's 3.2.
The baseline is Duktape 1.2.2, much older than Duktape 2.x; against a modern JavaScript interpreter such as QuickJS no comparison exists in the evidence.

Reference counting means cycles (a table that refers to itself, closures captured in their own environment) leak unless the host calls sq_collectgarbage, or forever if built with NO_GARBAGE_COLLECTOR.

Integer arithmetic is plain C++ on SQInteger with no overflow checks (32-bit unless _SQ64, which 64-bit builds define automatically). The integer fast path for '/' in SQVM::Execute (_ARITH_NOZERO) only tests for a zero divisor, so the INT_MIN / -1 guard in ARITH_OP is skipped, and that guard and the '%' one compare against the 32-bit INT_MIN even in 64-bit builds; a script dividing the minimum integer by -1 can therefore hit a hardware divide trap (read from source, not run).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Squirrel over AngelScript when you want dynamic typing with classes and coroutines and no GC pauses; pick AngelScript for statically typed, C++-like scripts with similar speed (2.039 s vs 2.126 s), mruby (2.098 s) for Ruby syntax, and Luau or Lua when speed or a maintained, fuzzed sandbox matters more. Gaijin's Quirrel fork (already noted as a seed lead) is a more actively developed descendant.
verified_claims_summary: In r-lyeh's Scriptorium (July 2015, AMD A10 3.8 GHz, Windows 7 64-bit, MSVC VS2015 RC or VS2013, both engines built /Ox /Oy /MT /DNDEBUG), whole-process time for recursive fib(34), averaged over 5 launches, was 2.126 s for Squirrel 3.0.7 versus 9.544 s for Duktape 1.2.2 in the same pass, about 4.5x (derived from page data; 3.5x in an earlier, noisier pass); PUC Lua at 1.341 s was about 1.6x faster than Squirrel.
status_note: MIT-licensed and copyable with 1.1k stars and vcpkg/Conan packages, but upstream maintenance is sporadic (last merge 2026-02-28, previous commits November 2024) and several 2026 memory-safety reports, including a sandbox-escape report, are open without a reply; the only speed evidence is one 2015 fib micro-benchmark against a 2015 Duktape.
